title: All Boys Aren't Blue
author: George M. Johnson
current_text: Flagler County School Board member Jill Woolbright filed a complaint with the Flagler County Sheriff’s Office alleging that All Boys Aren’t Blue violated state obscenity laws; the office found no criminal wrongdoing by Flagler Schools employees who added the book to school libraries. The North Kansas City School District removed All Boys Aren’t Blue from school library shelves, after which students launched a petition protesting the action.

sources.quote: Flagler County School Board member Jill Woolbright has filed a report with the Sheriff’s Office claiming a book that was on the shelves in three district schools violates state obscenity laws. Woolbright said she recently became aware that four copies of the book, “All Boys Aren’t Blue,” by George M. Johnson, were available in the media centers of the three schools
sources.title: School Board member Jill Woolbright turns to Sheriff's Office over 'obscene' book at schools | Observer Local News | Palm Coast Observer and Ormond Beach Observer

sources.quote: After reviewing a complaint filed on November 9th, the Flagler County Sheriff’s Office has found that no Flagler Schools employee committed criminal wrongdoing by adding All Boys Aren’t Blue by George M. Johnson into Flagler school libraries. The complaint, filed by School Board member Jill Woolbright, saw the community starkly divided over whether Johnson’s book constituted pornography, and whether someone should be held accountable for its presence in schools.
sources.title: FCSO Investigation Finds No Wrongdoing by Employees Who Added 'All Boys Aren't Blue' to School Libraries - AskFlagler

sources.quote: Concerns about the book have been raised by parents around the country. On Wednesday, Nov. 10, the Kansas City Star reported that after the North Kansas City School District removed “All Boys Aren’t Blue” and another book from school library shelves, students launched a petition to protest the actions.
